cases.note: The customer's name is an exact match for a listed person, and an officer's note mentions a brother born on the listed date of birth. Under the policy only the customer's own facts count. The small model compared the customer's own date of birth, recorded the conflict, and did not let the brother's date stand in for it. The large model was not called.

Only the name is captured. The small model names what is missing and the router stops there, because a larger model cannot supply a date of birth or a passport number that is not in the file. The output is a request for documents, routed to further investigation.

cases.tab: A correction, and what it reveals
cases.note: The small model read a place of birth marked not captured as a conflict. Asked to repair the policy error the checks found, it made its disposition agree with that wrong comparison: insufficient evidence. The router escalated on an observable reason, an agreement and a conflict side by side, and the large model got it right. With the small model alone this case ended as a needless stop in all three runs. A one-line rule in code (an attribute marked not captured cannot conflict) would fix it without any large-model call.
